title: $27 Million From 2,000 Seniors: The Fake Refund Trick

lines.say: More than twenty-seven million dollars from about two thousand seniors. One of the most frequent tricks: a refund that never existed.
lines.show: More than $27 million from about 2,000 seniors. One of the most frequent tricks: a refund that never existed.

lines.say: A call or pop-up says you're owed a small refund. Then the caller pretends to over-refund you by accident.
Send back the difference, they say. In cash, by express mail.
There was no refund. Victims sent their own money, to couriers with fake IDs.
One courier, Jiandong Chen, just got seventy-eight months.
lines.show: One courier, Jiandong Chen, just got 78 months.

lines.say: Has your family gotten this call? Tell me below.
